Make a group of ten counters. Fill the ten frame, one counter in each space.

steps.hint: Tap each object once. A marked object has already been counted.
steps.explanation: Count each object once, say how many altogether, and make a group of ten.
steps.shortExplanation: Make, count or compare the objects. Explain what changed.

mathWorkshop.title: Count for Owl
mathWorkshop.goal: Count each object once, say how many altogether, and make a group of ten.

tasks.prompt: Tap each apple once to count the apples for Owl.
tasks.feedback: You counted each apple once. Seven is the last count, so there are seven apples altogether.
tasks.hint: Tap each object once. A marked object has already been counted.

tasks.prompt: The same seven apples are spread out. None joined or left. How many now?
tasks.feedback: Still seven! Moving apples changes where they are, not how many there are.
tasks.hint: Think about whether an apple joined or left. You may count again to check.

tasks.prompt: Make a group of ten counters. Fill the ten frame, one counter in each space.
tasks.feedback: Ten counters fill all ten spaces. The number ten tells us how many altogether.
tasks.hint: Each space holds one counter. Count the filled spaces before checking.

parentReview.en: Guided practice is ungraded. Completion records the child doing the activities, not a book-question score.

steps.title: Maths discovery 2
steps.prompt: Count the apples. How many are there?
steps.hint: Touch each object once, then remember the last number.
steps.explanation: Touch each apple once. There are 8 apples.
steps.shortExplanation: Touch each apple once. There are 8 apples.

steps.title: Maths discovery 3
steps.prompt: Count the stars. How many are there?
steps.hint: Touch each object once, then remember the last number.
steps.explanation: Counting each star once gives 13 stars.
steps.shortExplanation: Counting each star once gives 13 stars.

steps.title: Maths discovery 4
steps.prompt: Fill the gaps in the number track.
steps.hint: Touch each object once, then remember the last number.

steps.title: Maths discovery 5
steps.prompt: Match each dot picture to its number.
steps.hint: Touch each object once, then remember the last number.

source.answerKeyText:
4, 6, 10. The dice pattern and the full ten frame should be known at a glance; if he counts
one by one, that's fine for now — play Game 2 again.

steps.title: Try it at home
steps.prompt: With an adult, draw 9 circles on paper. Count them together.
steps.hint: Touch each object once, then remember the last number.
steps.explanation: Try it with an adult. Talk about what you found.
steps.shortExplanation: Try it with an adult. Talk about what you found.

source.answerKeyText: Nine circles. Count them with him; check he didn't draw 10.

parentReview.en: Nine circles. Count them with him; check he didn't draw 10.
parentReview.note: Discuss with an adult; this personal or drawing response is not automatically graded.

steps.title: Maths discovery 7
steps.prompt: Sara spreads out 6 cups. Now there are more than 6 cups.
steps.hint: Touch each object once, then remember the last number.
steps.explanation: Moving the cups does not change how many there are.
steps.shortExplanation: Moving the cups does not change how many there are.

source.answerKeyText: False. There are still 6 cups — moving them doesn't make more.

steps.title: Maths discovery 8
steps.hint: Touch each object once, then remember the last number.
steps.explanation: Twelve is ten and two, written 12.
steps.shortExplanation: Twelve is ten and two, written 12.

source.answerKeyText: 12. If he circles 21, say "twelve is ten and two — the ten comes first."

steps.title: Try it at home
steps.prompt: Count something in your room with an adult. What did you count, and how many?
steps.hint: Touch each object once, then remember the last number.
steps.explanation: Try it with an adult. Talk about what you found.
steps.shortExplanation: Try it with an adult. Talk about what you found.

source.answerKeyText: Any real object and a correct count, e.g. "I counted my cars, there were 9."

parentReview.en: Any real object and a correct count, e.g. "I counted my cars, there were 9."
parentReview.note: Discuss with an adult; this personal or drawing response is not automatically graded.

steps.title: Maths discovery 10
steps.prompt: The last number you say when you count tells you...
steps.hint: Touch each object once, then remember the last number.
steps.explanation: How many altogether is the answer. The last count names the whole group.
steps.shortExplanation: How many altogether is the answer. The last count names the whole group.

steps.title: Maths discovery 11
steps.hint: Touch each object once, then remember the last number.
steps.explanation: 16 is the answer. Counting on one moves from 15 to 16.
steps.shortExplanation: 16 is the answer. Counting on one moves from 15 to 16.

steps.title: Maths discovery 12
steps.prompt: How many dots fill a whole ten frame?
steps.hint: Touch each object once, then remember the last number.
steps.explanation: 10 is the answer. A ten frame has ten spaces.
steps.shortExplanation: 10 is the answer. A ten frame has ten spaces.

steps.title: Maths discovery 13
steps.hint: Touch each object once, then remember the last number.
steps.explanation: 13 is the answer. Thirteen is ten and three.
steps.shortExplanation: 13 is the answer. Thirteen is ten and three.

steps.title: Maths discovery 14
steps.prompt: 5 spoons were in a pile. Now they are in a long line. How many spoons are there?
steps.hint: Touch each object once, then remember the last number.
steps.explanation: 5 is the answer. Moving a group does not change its number.
steps.shortExplanation: 5 is the answer. Moving a group does not change its number.

stickers.meaning: Say one number for each thing, in order.

homeActivities.text: Count 7 spoons while moving each once. Spread them out and ask whether the number changed. Play a short dice-dot guessing game.
